subject: Atria HealthTech — eval kickoff, dataset format & benchmark plan
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@atriahealthtech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atria HealthTech — post-call: dataset format + quick plan for model-fit eval

Hi Samantha — great to meet you on the call this morning. Quick recap and concrete next steps so we can get your customer-specific eval running on Redwood: 

Recap (2 min):
- Primary goal: evaluate whether an LLM can reliably extract structured risk-attributes from triage notes and surface candidate care-path suggestions with >85% QA acceptance.
- Hard constraints: PHI-masked dataset (you confirmed), 30k sample records for the first run, and a 2-week turnaround target for an initial benchmark.

What we need from Atria to start the run:
1) A 10–30k sample CSV (see required columns below) — please pseudonymize PHI before sending. 
2) A short prompt bank with 10 canonical examples (we can supplement). JSONL is ideal. 
3) Scoring rubric: we propose token-level field extraction F1 + human preference on 100 random cases. See suggested weights below.

Suggested models for initial shortlist (we'll run multi-model comparisons):
- Redwood-13B-Int8 (balance of cost & latency) — good baseline for structured extraction. 
- Redwood-7B-QAT (very low cost, check for recall drop on long notes). 
- Llama2-13b-chat (open-model baseline) — for parity comparison. 

Proposed scoring & pass criteria (we can adjust):
- Field extraction F1 (weighted average across 8 target fields) — 60% weight. Threshold: >=0.82 for green.
- Human preference trials (pairwise A/B blind) on 100 cases — 20% weight.
- Safety/regression checks (policy flags per example) — 20% weight (must be zero critical policy failures).

Required CSV columns (exact names):
- record_id (string), note_text (string), gold_entities (JSON-encoded list), gold_recommendation (string), source_system (string), pseudo_patient_id (string)

Attachments: I attached a benchmark mapping template and a prompt bank example; you can replace fields. If you prefer, upload to the Drive link and share editor access.

Next steps / calendar:
- Samantha: share sample CSV + 10 example prompts by Thurs 5/27.
- Redwood (Ben & Marissa): stand up a private eval run once sample arrives; target initial run start 5/28 and report 6/03.

If the timeline is tight we can run a fast 2k-record smoke test within 48 hours of receiving data — good for quick model triage. Let me know which you'd prefer.

Thanks — looking forward.

Best,
Logan Wright
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: benchmark-mapping.xlsx)
(attachment: prompt_bank_v1.jsonl)

From: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@atriahealthtech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Nikhil Rao <nikhil.rao@atriahealthtech.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 08:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atria HealthTech — post-call: dataset format + quick plan for model-fit eval

Thanks Logan — appreciate the clear plan. Quick answers and what we're attaching: 

- We'll deliver a 12k-row pseudonymized CSV by EOD Thurs (5/27). Attached is a small sample (atria_sample_hl_dataset.csv) with the exact columns you listed. We redacted names and MRNs.
- Prompt bank: we'll include 12 examples in JSONL format (attached).
- Scoring: we agree to your 60/20/20 split for the initial run. One tweak — can we increase the human-review sample to 150 cases? We do heavy manual QA on edge cases and prefer slightly bigger human checks.

Also noted the model shortlist — curious if Redwood-15B-int8 is on the table? We have compute budget for a slightly higher-sized trial if it materially improves recall. Can Ben advise on expected delta?

Confirming: we'll upload the full CSV and prompt JSONL to the Drive folder and also attach via email. Expect the upload by 5/27 17:00 PT.

Thanks,
Samantha Reed
Head of Data Science | Atria HealthTech
(attachment: atria_sample_hl_dataset.csv)
(attachment: prompt_bank_v1.jsonl)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@atriahealthtech.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 11:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atria HealthTech — post-call: dataset format + quick plan for model-fit eval

Great notes, Samantha — thanks for the sample. Quick responses to your two asks: 

1) Redwood-15B-Int8: yes, we can include that model in the comparison. Expect measurable recall uplift on multi-field extraction problems, usually +4–8% F1 vs 13B at similar prompt engineering. Cost will be ~1.7x of 13B for token compute. If you'd like, we can gate the 15B run to only the final 5k subset to control spend and still get representative signal. 

2) Human review sample size: 150 is fine — we'll use that for the A/B blind trials.

Operational notes for dataset you attached: your gold_entities column uses a pipe-separated string — that's OK, but please confirm whether nested entities exist (we'll treat nested as separate fields). Also saw ~120 samples with notes >2,500 chars; we may truncate at 2,000 for the initial 13B pass and run a targeted 15B pass for the long-tail. 

I'll put a short run plan in the Drive and trigger the benchmark once we get the full CSV. Logan / Marissa will provision a private eval job under your tenant and share the run link.

Best,
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
(attachment: benchmark-run-plan.txt)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Reed <samantha.reed@atriahealthtech.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 May 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atria HealthTech — post-call: dataset format + quick plan for model-fit eval

Samantha — thanks, the Drive upload is visible and I've confirmed access. Next concrete items from Redwood ops: 

- We'll provision the private eval environment under your org id RDW-ATR-2027-004 on 5/28 morning PT. Expect an automated pre-check report within 2 hours after provisioning (format validation, sample size, truncation stats).
- Default scoring runs (13B and 7B) will complete within 36 hours of run start; 15B gated run on long notes will be a separate job and we suggest scheduling it for 5/31 if you want to limit spend.
- Deliverables: a consolidated benchmark report (CSV of per-record outputs + aggregated metrics), a short slide deck with model recommendations and tradeoffs, and a blind human-preference packet for the 150-case review.

I'll include run owners and expected cost estimate in the Drive doc. If you want expedited turnaround on the 15B across full corpus, ping me and I can escalate for a one-off quote. 

See you on the quick sync Monday — if anything changes with the dataset format (nested entities or a different field name) please flag before provisioning.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Manager, Customer Solutions | Redwood Inference
(attachment: run-output-template.csv)
